newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 26.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page on March 26:

BEIJING - Vice President Gore promised Chinese Premier Li Peng Tuesday that allegations that Beijing may have tried to buy influence in Washingtion with illegal campaign contributions will not affect the Clinton administration's policy of seeking warmer relations with China.
WASHINGTON - The Federal Reserve, concerned that inflation will begin to increase later this year, raised interest rates yesterday to try to keep that from happening.

WINGATE, N.C. - Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms, standing next to Secretary of State Madeleine K. Albright in another meeting between the two, signalled today that he will allow an international treaty banning chemical weapons to come to a ratification vote in the Senate.

MIAMI - Moments after convicted killer Pedro Medina was strapped into Florida's electric chair and 2,000 volts of electricity surged into his body this morning, flames leapt from the inmate's head, filling the death chamber with smoke and horrifying two dozen witnesses.

WASHINGTON - Montgomery County police were holding one man last night and searching for another suspect in the so-called Brit Bandit robberies, a series of home break-ins over the last two months that have frightened and bemused some of the county's pricier neighbourhoods.

WASHINGTON - The Maryland General Assembly has defied the federal government and Gov. Parris N. Glendening by voting to scuttle an expanded mandatory vehicle-emissions test -- a move that could lead to federal sanctions, including the loss of nearly $100 million in highway construction funds.
